case_name: Smt. Narinder Pal Kaur Chawla vs Shri Manjeet Singh Chawla
facts_of_case: The respondent, who was already married to one Amarjeet Kaur, pretended to be a bachelor and married the appellant. The couple lived together for several years before the respondent deserted the appellant. The appellant filed a petition under Sections 18 and 20 of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act claiming recovery of maintenance and right of residence from the respondent.

legal_principles.principle: A woman in the position of the appellant can seek maintenance.
legal_principles.held: We are of the opinion that the legislature never intended that a woman like the appellant, in which position she is placed, be not treated as the 'wife' of the respondent at least for the purposes of Section 18 of the Act and be deprived of her right to seek maintenance.
cited_cases: Savitaben Somabhai Bhatiya, (Year) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: A court may entertain an appeal against an order fixing interim maintenance if the quantum is extremely low.
legal_principles.held: Normally, this Court would not have entertained this appeal as it is directed against an order fixing only interim maintenance pending adjudication of claim of maintenance by the wife under the Act: On the prima facie evidence with regard to the social and financial status of the parties, this Court finds that interim maintenance of Rs. 700/- per month fixed by the Division Bench of the High Court is extremely low.

outcome.final_order: The Court ordered the respondent to pay interim maintenance to the appellant, with varying amounts over time.

use_for_drafting: advising on marriage and family law
